```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The planning LP in algebra</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

For each hour $t$ of the six days, with weight $w_t$ (the days it stands for); each step lasts one hour, so $x$ MW for an hour is $x$ MWh:

$$\min\; \sum_{k} C_k X_k + \sum_t w_t \big( c_{cc}\,\mathit{cc}_t + c_{ct}\,\mathit{ct}_t + V\,u_t \big)$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathit{we}_t + \mathit{se}_t + \mathit{wn}_t + \mathit{sn}_t + \mathit{cc}_t + \mathit{ct}_t + d_t - c_t + u_t &= D_t && \text{(balance)}\\
\mathit{wn}_t \le f^w_t\, W, \quad \mathit{sn}_t \le f^s_t\, S, \quad c_t, d_t \le B, \quad e_t &\le 4B && \text{(sizes)}\\
\mathit{we}_t \le \bar w_t, \quad \mathit{se}_t \le \bar s_t, \quad \mathit{cc}_t \le 2{,}000, \quad \mathit{ct}_t &\le 2{,}300 && \text{(what exists)}\\
W, S \le 8{,}000, \quad B &\le 4{,}000 && \text{(build limits)}\\
e_t = e_{t-1} + 0.85\, c_t - d_t &&& \text{(battery; each day ends with the energy it began with)}\\
\sum_t w_t \big( r_{cc}\,\mathit{cc}_t + r_{ct}\,\mathit{ct}_t \big) &\le \varepsilon && \text{(the cap)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Every variable is zero or more.

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $X_k$, $C_k$ | new wind $W$, solar $S$, battery $B$; each one's yearly capital and upkeep | MW; \$ per MW a year |
| $\mathit{we}, \mathit{se}, \mathit{wn}, \mathit{sn}$ | existing and new wind and solar used | MW |
| $\bar w_t$, $\bar s_t$ | what the existing wind and solar could make that hour | MW |
| $\mathit{cc}$, $\mathit{ct}$ | output of the gas combined-cycle plants and of the gas peakers (combustion turbines) | MW |
| $c_{cc}$, $c_{ct}$; $r_{cc}$, $r_{ct}$ | their running cost and CO₂ per MWh | \$/MWh; t/MWh |
| $c_t, d_t, e_t$ | battery charge, discharge and energy | MW; MW; MWh |
| $u_t$ | unserved demand | MW |
| $V$ | the value of lost load, \$10,000 | \$/MWh |
| $f^w_t$, $f^s_t$, $D_t$ | capacity factors per MW, and demand | share; MW |
| $\varepsilon$ | the cap | t a year |

- **A price** $\tau$ drops the cap and adds $\tau \sum_t w_t (r_{cc}\,\mathit{cc}_t + r_{ct}\,\mathit{ct}_t)$ to the goal.
- **Hourly matching** adds the buyer's own $W_b, S_b, B_b$ and, every hour, $\mathit{wb}_t + \mathit{sb}_t + d^b_t - c^b_t \ge 300$, with $c^b_t \le \mathit{wb}_t + \mathit{sb}_t$.
- **Annual matching** keeps one row: $\sum_t w_t (\mathit{wb}_t + \mathit{sb}_t) \ge 300 \times 8{,}760$.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Caps, prices and ties</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **One dual, checked by finite steps.** The test loosens and tightens each cap by 1,000 t; the cost changes at the dual's rate both ways. That is a sensitivity check, not a proof.
- **A positive dual means the cap binds in every best plan.** This is complementary slackness: a rule with a nonzero dual holds exactly. So the cap's CO₂ is the same for all of them, though their schedules may differ.
- **A price ties a stretch.** Where the frontier is straight, a price equal to the magnitude of its downward slope makes every plan on that stretch score the same; the solver returns one of them.
- **So report the range.** The page solves twice more at each price, for the least and the most CO₂ among the best plans, and shows the range when they differ.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>

<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Six days against the full year</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<!-- m06-fullyear:start (written from the model by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<ul>
<li><b>Annual matching.</b> On all 8,760 hours of 2025 the 844 MW of wind make 95% of the data center's load over the year: the six weighted days were windier than the year.</li>
<li><b>Hourly matching.</b> Run hour by hour through 2025, the portfolio leaves at least 290 MWh unmatched, 0.01% of the load's year, in hours of low wind and sun. Which hours carry it can differ between equally good schedules.</li>
<li><b>So:</b> a rule met on representative days is a representative-day result. Check it on the full year, as the notebook does.</li>
</ul>
<!-- m06-fullyear:end -->
</div>
</details>
```

```{=html}
<!-- m06-check:start (written from the model by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="m6-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="price-cap" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A carbon price equal to a cap's dual gives back exactly the cap's plan.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. At the 70% cap's dual ($22.81 per t, rounded; the tie needs its full precision), every plan from 3.15 Mt to 3.64 Mt scores the same. The cap's plan is one of them.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="hourly-cut" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If a buyer's purchases let it claim zero emissions, the plants emit no more than without it.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. With certificates from existing wind the data center claims 0 t, and the plants emit +1.14 Mt a year more.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="dual-rise" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “In an LP, the cost of cutting one more tonne never falls as the cap tightens.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. The LP's frontier is convex: here the dual rises from $21.98 at 90% to $130.61 at 30%.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="m6">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="dual" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">A cap's dual is $22.81 per t. Loosening the cap by 1,000 t changes the best cost by about how much?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">It rises by about $22,810</li><li data-value="b">It falls by about $22,810</li><li data-value="c">It falls by $22.81</li><li data-value="d">Nothing: the dual is only a price</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>It falls by about $22,810: $22.81 × 1,000 t, the dual rounded to the cent, while the cap stays in the dual's range.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<p class="lx-eyebrow">In the real world</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:ghg"><p>Reductions are computed under average-emission-intensity accounting with perfect foresight; they are not estimates of the consequential (marginal) system response.</p><footer>Approved excerpt of: Li et al. (2025), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crsus.2025.100367">Cell Reports Sustainability</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Case file <a href="cf6-shifting-load-to-clean-hours.html">CF6</a>: how much shifting load to cleaner hours can cut emissions, and when.</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:txh2"><p>A two-stage stochastic linear program sized electrolyzers, hydrogen tanks and fuel cells once in each of ERCOT's eight weather zones, with hydrogen pipelines between neighbouring zones, then scheduled the system hour by hour over a full year in nine scenarios: three completion rates of planned renewable capacity by three electricity-demand levels.</p><p>When gas-fired backup power became much more expensive, the model built fuel cells and turned stored green hydrogen back into electricity.</p><p>Industry then drew more hydrogen from gas reformers, and the round trip from power to hydrogen and back lost energy, so total emissions rose although gas-plant emissions fell.</p><footer>Approved excerpt of: Li et al. (2025), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhydene.2025.02.303">International Journal of Hydrogen Energy</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Inputs reflect 2022–2023 conditions; post-2023 federal hydrogen credit rules are not modeled.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Case file <a href="cf3-hydrogen-under-uncertainty.html">CF3</a>: where hydrogen should go when nobody knows how much wind will be built.</p>
<div class="lx-case-try">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Try it yourself</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Optional, about 30 minutes; needs Python on your computer (<a href="b02-python-data.html">lesson B2</a>).</p>
<ul>
<li>Write the synthetic regions with <code>ghg-framework synthetic my_inputs/</code>, then run <code>ghg-framework run my_inputs/ --region Mixed --limit 0.08 --lam 5 --out-dir outputs/mixed</code>.</li>
<li>Its goal counts each hour at its average intensity. Write down what you would change to count the change at the plants instead, as question 2 of A10 does.</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://github.com/Henryutd2021/ghg-load-regulation">ghg-load-regulation</a>: public example repository · MIT licence · synthetic data.</p>
</div>
</div>
```
